## Research question
How does Bramblewood compare with Larkspur-Seq in NDCG@10 on the Brightcart-Grocery dataset?

## Methods summary
Bramblewood is a session-based recommender that builds an item-transition graph for each session and scores candidate items with a gated graph encoder. Larkspur-Seq, a self-attentive sequential recommender, is the strongest baseline in our study; Most-Popular, which recommends globally popular items, is a non-personalized reference.

## Experimental setup
Models are trained on the first 26 days of Brightcart-Grocery logs (1.2M sessions) and evaluated on sessions from the final 4 days (61,400 sessions) with leave-last-item-out next-item prediction over the full item catalogue. Hyperparameters were tuned on a validation split from the training period. Bramblewood and Larkspur-Seq were each trained with 10 random seeds (seeds 0–9); seed i fixes initialization and mini-batch order for both models, so their seed-level scores are paired. Most-Popular is deterministic.

## Experiments and comparisons
- `exp1`: Next-item prediction on the Brightcart-Grocery test period
  - comparison `exp1/cmp1`: Bramblewood vs Larkspur-Seq, NDCG@10
  - comparison `exp1/cmp2`: Bramblewood vs Most-Popular, NDCG@10

## Results tables

sentences.text: On the Brightcart-Grocery test set, Bramblewood achieved a mean NDCG@10 of 41.2% (SD 0.7) across 10 seeds, compared to 40.7% (SD 0.6) for Larkspur-Seq.

The observed mean difference was 0.5 percentage points; because seeds are paired, a paired test could assess reliability, but none was reported, so this cannot be interpreted as a reliable improvement.
Bramblewood's mean NDCG@10 was 22.9 points higher than Most-Popular's 18.3%.
These results are specific to Brightcart-Grocery and the leave-last-item-out protocol.

On the Brightcart-Grocery test period, Bramblewood achieved a higher mean NDCG@10 (41.2% ± 0.7%) than Larkspur-Seq (40.7% ± 0.6%), although no statistical test was reported, so this difference cannot be claimed as significant.
Bramblewood's mean NDCG@10 was also substantially higher than the deterministic Most-Popular baseline (18.3%).
Bramblewood similarly showed higher mean Recall@20 (63.8% ± 0.8%) than both Larkspur-Seq (63.1% ± 0.8%) and Most-Popular (37.9%), again without a reported significance test.
On the Brightcart-Grocery test set, Bramblewood achieved a mean NDCG@10 of 41.2% (SD 0.7) across 10 seeds, compared to 40.7% (SD 0.6) for Larkspur-Seq.
This corresponds to a mean improvement of 0.5 percentage points for Bramblewood over Larkspur-Seq, but no statistical test was reported, so the difference cannot be characterized as significant.

Both neural models scored higher than the non-personalized Most-Popular baseline, which reached an NDCG@10 of 18.3% (Bramblewood 41.2%, Larkspur-Seq 40.7%); no statistical test was reported for this comparison.
